scope: Composable maintained obligations for statistical inference and uncertainty engineering. They encode bounded cross-domain failure classes and selected domain adapters, not every discipline, estimator, model, interval, regulator, venue, or decision threshold.

obligations: Define the scientific question, estimand or target quantity, analysis population, independent unit, estimator, estimate, and uncertainty semantics before binding quantitative claims.
Report effect magnitude, typed uncertainty, denominators, method, deviations, and relevant adverse, harmful, null, failed, and inconclusive results without treating a threshold as scientific truth.
transfer_limits: Does not select a best estimator, model, interval, threshold, or evidential framework; exact domain and venue rules remain live research.

obligations: Bind randomized assignment, analysis populations, primary and secondary outcomes, harms, missingness, multiplicity, analysis timing, and deviations to the protocol and executed analysis.
Preserve intention-to-treat or other declared population semantics and expose exclusions and denominator changes.
transfer_limits: Clinical-trial and biomedical reporting rules are not universal design requirements for every randomized experiment; resolve regulator and venue rules exactly.

obligations: State target population, exposure/outcome timing, confounding strategy, missingness assumptions, selection mechanisms, and whether the objective is descriptive, associational, predictive, or causal.
Keep measured adjustment from certifying causal identification and report sensitivity boundaries and deviations.
transfer_limits: STROBE improves reporting but does not validate causal identification; exact design-specific identification assumptions require live domain expertise.

obligations: Identify index and reference tests, target condition, participant spectrum, thresholds, indeterminate results, analysis set, and uncertainty for diagnostic accuracy estimates.
Do not transfer discrimination-only evidence into calibration, clinical utility, or downstream-outcome claims.
transfer_limits: Diagnostic accuracy does not by itself establish clinical utility, transportability, or treatment benefit.

obligations: Bind prediction target, time horizon, development and validation populations, split or resampling design, leakage controls, calibration, discrimination, utility, subgroup assessment, and uncertainty.
Report relevant sources of training/evaluation variance and do not let one aggregate score establish calibration, utility, fairness, robustness, or deployment readiness.
transfer_limits: Clinical prediction guidance and benchmark studies do not define a universal model, metric, fairness rule, or deployment threshold.

obligations: Bind eligibility, effect measure, study-level estimates, synthesis model, heterogeneity, missing results, sensitivity analyses, and protocol deviations.
Use a prediction interval when making a supported claim about effects in a future setting and distinguish it from uncertainty around a pooled mean.
transfer_limits: Review-reporting and intervention meta-analysis guidance does not validate search completeness, exchangeability, bias adjustment, or every synthesis model.

obligations: Identify the experimental unit, biological versus technical replication, group allocation, exclusions, blinding, sample-size rationale, outcomes, harms, and dependence.
Do not report subsamples, wells, fields, sections, or repeated measurements as independent n.
transfer_limits: ARRIVE is a reporting framework, not proof of rigor or a universal prescription for every organism and design.

obligations: Bind specimen and batch structure, preprocessing, filtering, feature universe, confirmatory or exploratory hypothesis family, multiplicity objective, stability, and validation.
Keep false-discovery control, family-wise error control, exploratory ranking, and external validation as distinct objectives.
transfer_limits: No universal preprocessing, filtering, batch-correction, or multiplicity method transfers across assays and objectives.

obligations: Specify aims, data-generating mechanisms, estimands, methods, performance measures, factors, simulation size, Monte Carlo uncertainty, failures, and code/environment receipts.
For empirical benchmarks, expose seeds, splits, repeated trials, tuning budgets, comparator parity, variance sources, and failed or adverse runs.
transfer_limits: ADEMP and ML reproducibility practices guide reporting; they do not establish representative scenarios, fair comparisons, or external validity universally.

obligations: Identify every observation, assignment, analysis, cluster, and independent unit and model, aggregate, or otherwise justify dependence handling.
Bind cluster counts and effective independent n separately from observation or subsample counts.
transfer_limits: No universal mixed-model structure or degrees-of-freedom method follows from detecting hierarchy; design and estimand determine the analysis.

obligations: Define time origin, endpoint, censoring, competing events, estimand, risk set, follow-up horizon, model or nonparametric method, and proportionality or other relevant diagnostics.
Expose numbers at risk, censoring or competing-event semantics, uncertainty, and late-follow-up instability where applicable.
transfer_limits: Kaplan-Meier, competing-risk, and model-based estimands are not interchangeable; exact endpoint and regulatory rules require live resolution.

obligations: Document likelihood, prior and prior predictive implications, computation, convergence and effective sample diagnostics, posterior summaries, posterior predictive checks, and sensitivity to consequential modeling choices.
Use correctly labeled credible or posterior predictive uncertainty; do not fabricate P values or reinterpret credible intervals as confidence intervals.
transfer_limits: No universal prior, Bayes-factor threshold, interval, convergence cutoff, or model-comparison rule applies to all Bayesian analyses.

obligations: Prospectively justify the smallest effect or noninferiority margin, direction, decision rule, analysis populations, interval convention, and consequences of assay sensitivity or protocol deviations.
Do not infer equivalence, noninferiority, or no meaningful effect from a nonsignificant difference test.
transfer_limits: Regulatory noninferiority and general equivalence objectives use context-specific margins and analysis conventions; neither transfers automatically.

obligations: Do not fabricate sample-size calculations, P values, confidence intervals, effect estimates, or quantitative uncertainty for a non-quantitative objective.

Resolve the appropriate qualitative, interpretive, historical, formal-proof, or domain-specific standards and preserve reflexivity, provenance, counterevidence, and bounded transfer claims where relevant.
transfer_limits: Qualitative reporting guidelines do not govern formal proof, historical argument, every interpretive tradition, or mixed-method quantitative components; resolve exact domain norms live.
